title: Nagata rings ascend along weakly etale Noetherian ring maps
statement: Let $A$ be a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $f:A\to B$ be weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Then $B$ is a Nagata ring. No universal catenarity or J-2 assumption is imposed on $A$.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Remark 5.7(ii), printed p. 148; Remark 5.2 identifies AF with weakly etale. The proof of Theorem 5.3(iii), printed p. 147, cites [4] for local Nagata ascent; Remark 5.7(ii) records the stronger global Nagata ascent.

proof.text: For a weakly etale k-algebra F over a field, use Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.of_flat_lmul' from WeilConjectures.RingTheory.ProEtale.WeakDimension. Every prime localization is therefore a field and hence a normal domain. For a k-algebra homomorphism F to a field E, localize at its kernel. The localization remains weakly etale. The theorem Algebra.WeaklyEtale.not_forall_isUnit_aeval forces each element of that field to be algebraic over k: otherwise every nonzero polynomial evaluated there would be a nonzero unit. Transport its algebraic relation to E. This proves the needed field-fibre assertions in arbitrary universes without ind-etale presentations.

source.place: Tag 092Q (lemma-absolutely-flat-over-field), with algebra.tex Tags 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral) and 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring); elementary inverse-polynomial calculation is written out Lean implementation uses the ring-level Mathlib and proved source-library APIs described in this step.

proof.text: Use the algebraic base-change instance Algebra.WeaklyEtale k (k tensor_A B), and map this tensor product into E = Frac(B/q). The preceding algebraic-image calculation shows the images of all b in B are algebraic over k = Frac(A/p). Every element of E is a quotient of such images, so E/k is algebraic. All algebra structures are constructed by quotient maps and the universal property of fraction fields. No scheme base-change comparison is needed.

source.place: Tag 094U (lemma-base-change-weakly-etale); schemes.tex Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); algebra.tex Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence). Fibre fractions are displayed explicitly Lean implementation uses the ring-level Mathlib and proved source-library APIs described in this step.

proof.text: For a finite extension L/E, transitivity makes L/k algebraic. Choose a finite E-algebra generating set s of L using Module.Finite.finiteType. The explicitly constructed intermediate field K = IntermediateField.adjoin k s is finite dimensional over k by IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_adjoin. Since its elements include s, Algebra.adjoin E K is all of L. This constructs the finite field model rather than choosing an undetermined normalization witness.

source.place: Elementary finite field model: choose equations for a finite E-basis, adjoin their algebraic coefficients over k, and use the bounded monomials to obtain a finite-dimensional domain, hence a field. This is the finite-normalization model argument, with no J-2 hypothesis. Lean implementation uses the ring-level Mathlib and proved source-library APIs described in this step.

proof.text: Put D = A/p and R = integralClosure D K. Nagata makes D N-2. To apply its same-universe quantifier to the possibly larger K, use Module.Finite.small and Shrink.algEquiv, then transport module finiteness of the integral closure along mapIntegralClosure. The normalization lemmas make R an integrally closed domain with fraction field K. It is Noetherian and finite over A. Localizations at primes are normal domains.

source.place: Tags 032R (definition-nagata), 032F (definition-N), 034L (lemma-integral-closure-in-normal), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain); fraction-field clause from the cited existing normalization node Lean implementation uses the ring-level Mathlib and proved source-library APIs described in this step.

proof.text: Set C = R tensor_A B, using the right B-algebra structure. Tensor-product finiteness makes C finite over B, hence Noetherian. Its R-algebra is weakly etale by algebraic base change, hence flat. Every fibre is weakly etale over its residue field and its prime localizations are fields by absolute flatness. Apply normal_of_flat_normal_fibers to conclude C is normal.

source.place: Tag 0C22 (lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian); the finite base-change spanning calculation is written out Lean implementation uses the ring-level Mathlib and proved source-library APIs described in this step.

proof.text: The compatible maps from R and B to L define h:C -> L by the tensor universal property. Its kernel Q avoids the image of every nonzero element of R. Localize C to K tensor_R C; this generic fibre is absolutely flat, so all its primes are maximal by Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.tfae. If a prime P is contained in Q, both avoid those denominators. Their extensions to the generic fibre are comparable primes, hence equal; extension-contraction gives P = Q. Thus Q is minimal.

source.place: Agent prime-ideal calculation from the zero-dimensional generic fibre established in step 2; compare Tag 092Q Lean implementation uses the ring-level Mathlib and proved source-library APIs described in this step.

proof.text: C is reduced by Mathlib isReduced_ofLocalizationMaximal, since its prime localizations are domains. Noetherianity gives finitely many minimal primes. Use reduced_normal_iff_integrallyClosed_totalFractions to write C as a finite product of normal domains. PrimeSpectrum.exists_comap_evalRingHom_eq selects a factor for Q; its evaluation kernel lies below Q and is prime, hence equals Q by minimality. The first isomorphism theorem makes C/Q integrally closed. Let T be the actual subalgebra h(C) of L over B/q. It is finite by the surjection from C. The same first isomorphism theorem transfers integral closedness to T. The subfield generated by T contains E and K by their fraction presentations, so contains Algebra.adjoin E K = L. The fraction-field lift then proves IsFractionRing T L.

source.place: Tags 00FR (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components) and 030C (lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal), together with the source of lem-weil-pbc-prime-localizations-jointly-injective; product-prime and fraction-field identifications are written out Lean implementation uses the ring-level Mathlib and proved source-library APIs described in this step.

proof.text: Every element of integralClosure (B/q) L is integral over T by IsIntegral.tower_top and belongs to T by integral closedness in its fraction field L. This defines an injective B/q-linear map of that integral closure into the finite B/q-module T. Since B/q is Noetherian, Module.Finite.of_injective proves finiteness of the integral closure. This proves N-2 for every prime quotient of B, hence Nagata. No primes exist when B is the zero ring, so that case is vacuous.

split_report.summary: Expanded the Nagata-ascent argument into eight complete steps. The route constructs finite normalizations after passing to residue fields, uses weak-etale field fibres and flat normal-fibre ascent to identify the integral closure, and concludes the Nagata condition for every prime quotient of B. The existing J-2 argument was intentionally omitted because it is not part of this item; no new support nodes were needed.
